growth_ceiling_reason: a doubling sentinel, not a byte budget. Five growth runs of one unmodified build came back at 192, 384, 422, 461 and 461 first-party bytes per extra visit per host (an earlier batch, divided by the library size read before the visits rather than after, spread 230 to 499). What moves is how many times the page reads the library during a visit and how many hosts discovery had added by then, neither of which this repository controls, so a ceiling at one graph per host per visit -- 384 -- would go red on the shipped code. The ceiling therefore sits above two graphs per visit per host (768, which still passes and is written down as the blind spot in the fixtures) and refuses at three (1152), which is what a second owner of the TemporaryHost/TemporaryApp cycle looks like rather than a busier render.
growth_graph_rule_reason: why the leaked graph count is judged as a slope over a long window and never as a count over a short one. `leaks` answers what is still orphaned at one instant after the app stops, so the number this rule reads is a snapshot of a population whose size at that instant depends on how recently each read ran and what had drained since, neither of which this repository owns. Measured with one host in the library on the shipped code: the one-visit sweep came back at 9 and 9 leaked graphs (CI 2026-09-24 run 36000138662, arm64 and x86_64), 9 and 9 (CI 2026-09-25 run 36051089381, both architectures), 6 on arm64 and 8 on x86_64 (CI 2026-09-25 run 36058010642), and 9 on the laptop; the difference between the one-visit and the six-visit sweep came back 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6 and 6 across those CI runs, and 3, 6, 7 and 7 across the laptop's four earlier sweeps read out of their byte totals at 384 bytes per graph (those four predate the read counter, so their read count is taken from the 2026-09-25 measurement of one read per visit rather than measured alongside them). The rule ad2d35a wrote -- the difference may not exceed reads x visits x hosts -- refused that same correct code twice on a runner (run 36058010642: 6 graphs against 5 entitled on arm64, 6 against 5 on x86_64) and once on the laptop, which is the signature of a rule that had started measuring the snapshot instead of the leak. So the window has to be long enough to carry a slope: fewer than growth_graph_rule_min_visits (10) extra visits are refused outright rather than judged, and the surplus is refused above growth_graph_count_ratio (1.6) times the read rate. 1.6 is measured rather than picked: the largest surplus ever recorded was 7 graphs against an entitled 5 (a ratio of 1.4), and the snapshot noise of about three graphs per sweep is 0.2 of slope once the window is 15 visits, so 1.6 covers every run on record while two graphs per visit per host -- the shape the rule exists to catch -- is refused at 60 against the 48 the ratio allows. The change tightened that case rather than loosening it: under the old rule a doubling of the graph rate was the recorded blind spot at five visits, and now it is a refusal. What this rule cannot see is a creator adding less than 60% on top of the read rate, which is kept as the case `the measured blind spot` in growth_fixture() so a future reader finds it in the fixtures.

ci_runner.byte_budget: judged in the seeded runs: 512 per leaked host plus a 128 floor, and both sat inside it (2,688 against 3,712, 2,304 against 3,200). Under the ceiling this file carried until that push, both runs would have been refused -- 24,416 against 19,500 and 23,424 against 17,000 -- which is the change of rule measured on a runner rather than argued at a desk
